subject: mathematics
question_text: If A, A₁, A₂, A₃ are the areas of the incircle and the three excircles of a triangle respectively, prove that 1/√A₁ + 1/√A₂ + 1/√A₃ = 1/√A.

mark_split.label: Write each area with its radius

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write each area with its radius
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. √(πr²) = r√π because every radius is positive, and the same √π appears in all four terms.
steps.memory_tip: √(πr²) = r√π. The √π is common to all four terms, so it cancels and only the radii matter.
lines: Here A, A₁, A₂, A₃ are AREAS, not angles.
Let r be the inradius and r₁, r₂, r₃ the exradii.
(a circle of radius ρ has area πρ²)
A = πr², A₁ = πr₁², A₂ = πr₂², A₃ = πr₃²
√A = r√π and √A₁ = r₁√π (same for r₂, r₃)

recall.must_convey: That A = πr² gives √A = r√π, so the whole statement reduces to one about 1/r₁ + 1/r₂ + 1/r₃ and 1/r.
accept: each area is pi r squared so its root is r root pi
the root pi is common to all four terms and cancels
the question becomes one over r one plus one over r two plus one over r three
pi r square ki root teeste r root pi vasthundi
take the root of each area and the radii are all that is left

steps.why: Each area is π times a square, so its square root is the radius times √π. The √π is the same in all four terms and can be taken out, which turns the question into one about the radii alone.
common_mistakes: Using the circumference 2πr in place of the area πr².

steps.label: Add the reciprocal radii
steps.margin_note: The other mark. (s−a) + (s−b) + (s−c) = 3s − 2s = s, so the three reciprocals add to s/Δ, which is 1/r.

lines.text: r_{1}\ = \ \dfrac{\Delta }{s - a},\ r_{2}\ = \ \dfrac{\Delta }{s - b},\ r_{3}\ = \ \dfrac{\Delta }{s - c}
(take the reciprocal of each; the denominator Δ is shared)

accept: invert each exradius so the numerators are s minus a s minus b and s minus c
they add to three s minus two s which is s
the sum is s over delta which is one over r
moodu kalipithe three s minus two s ante s vasthundi
the reciprocals of the three exradii add to one over the inradius

steps.why: Inverting each exradius makes the numerators (s−a), (s−b) and (s−c), and those three add to 3s − 2s = s. That is exactly s/Δ, which is 1/r.
common_mistakes: Adding (s−a) + (s−b) + (s−c) and getting 2s instead of s.

lines_compact.text: r_{1}\ = \ \dfrac{\Delta }{s - a},\ r_{2}\ = \ \dfrac{\Delta }{s - b},\ r_{3}\ = \ \dfrac{\Delta }{s - c}
